question: An online clothes shop's product pages showed almost only four- and five-star reviews. What had it been doing?
answer: Holding back the poor reviews. In 2022 the US Federal Trade Commission found Fashion Nova had, for about four years, left hundreds of thousands of reviews under four stars unpublished; the firm paid $4.2 million. Every review shown was genuine, and the picture they made together was still false.
move: A collection of true parts can still tell a false story.
ask: Is there a story I tell about my life, or my work, using only the good reviews?
trap: Fake reviews are the familiar fraud, so the shop must have written them.
source: Federal Trade Commission, Fashion Nova case, 2022
reference: Federal Trade Commission, press release on the Fashion Nova review suppression settlement, 25 January 2022
